surface: Headless editor surface: BlockNoteViewRaw, BlockNoteViewEditor, BlockNoteContext/useBlockNoteContext, useCreateBlockNote, useBlockNoteEditor, useEditorChange, useEditorSelectionChange, usePrefersColorScheme. Default UI and custom React specs are out of scope.
divergences: No default UI: BlockNoteView, BlockNoteDefaultUI, ComponentsContext, and toolbar/menu/side-menu/table-handle/comment components are not provided. BlockNoteViewRaw matches upstream rendered without a components context.
BlockNoteViewRaw accepts no default UI flags, and portalElements reads only `default`.
Custom React block, inline content, and style specs are not provided.
Handlers receive native DOM events rather than React synthetic events.
ssr: Server rendering emits the BlockNoteViewRaw shell (container and empty editor host) without touching the DOM; the editor mounts on the client. usePrefersColorScheme uses a no-preference server snapshot, so server HTML and hydration agree on the light fallback and the live system scheme applies after hydration. Covered by the blocknote-ssr (Node) and blocknote-hydration projects.
notes: Independently authored MIT adapter. @blocknote/react is MPL-2.0 and none of its source is vendored or adapted; see UPSTREAM.md.
@blocknote/core is reused unchanged as a runtime dependency and supplies @blocknote/core/style.css.
Conformance tests mount real BlockNote editors in jsdom for view rendering, onChange, editable remounts, renderEditor=false placement, and unmount.
useCreateBlockNote still constructs the editor during server render, matching upstream; construction needs no DOM and the instance is discarded with the request.

Published types reach @blocknote/core → @shikijs/types, which uses Symbol.dispose. Consumers need lib esnext.disposable (or ES2025+) or skipLibCheck; the strict ES2024 browser consumer check lists this in packedTsrxSourceExceptions, like @octanejs/lexical.
